cases.title: Empty object is a JSON text
cases.paragraph: An object structure is represented as a pair of curly brackets surrounding zero or more name/value pairs.

cases.title: Empty array is a JSON text
cases.paragraph: An array structure is represented as square brackets surrounding zero or more values.

cases.title: Object with string, number, bool, null, nested array
cases.paragraph: An object is an unordered collection of zero or more name/value pairs.

cases.title: Array may mix JSON types
cases.paragraph: There is no requirement that the values in an array be of the same type.

cases.title: Standard escape sequences
cases.paragraph: All Unicode characters may be placed within quotation marks except those that must be escaped: quotation mark, reverse solidus, and the control characters. Short escapes include \", \\, \/, \b, \f, \n, \r, \t, and \uXXXX.

cases.title: Unicode code point via \u and literal UTF-8
cases.paragraph: Any code point may be represented as a hexadecimal escape; UTF-8 is the interchange encoding of the text.

cases.title: Integer without leading zero
cases.paragraph: A number contains an integer component that may be prefixed with a minus sign.

cases.title: Fractional number with exponent
cases.paragraph: A number may have a fractional part and/or an exponent part.

cases.title: Insignificant whitespace around a value
cases.paragraph: Whitespace may be inserted between any pair of tokens.

cases.title: A JSON text may be a string
cases.paragraph: A JSON text is a serialized value. Note that this is different from RFC 4627, which allowed only object or array at the top level.

cases.title: A JSON text may be a number
cases.paragraph: A JSON text is a serialized value.

cases.title: A JSON text may be true
cases.paragraph: A JSON value MUST be an object, array, number, or string, or one of the literal names true, false, or null.

cases.title: A JSON text may be null
cases.paragraph: A JSON value MUST be an object, array, number, or string, or one of the literal names true, false, or null.

cases.title: Trailing comma after the last object member is invalid
cases.paragraph: A JSON value is object / array / number / string / true / false / null. A trailing comma is not in the grammar.

cases.title: Trailing comma after the last array element is invalid
cases.paragraph: A JSON value is object / array / number / string / true / false / null. A trailing comma is not in the grammar.

cases.title: Single-quoted strings are not JSON
cases.paragraph: A string begins and ends with quotation mark (U+0022), not apostrophe.

cases.title: C-style comments are not JSON
cases.paragraph: The JSON grammar has no comment production.

cases.title: NaN is not a JSON number
cases.paragraph: Numeric values are produced from the number grammar; NaN is not a number token.

cases.title: Infinity is not a JSON number
cases.paragraph: Numeric values that cannot be represented as sequences of digits (such as Infinity and NaN) are not permitted.

cases.title: Leading zeros are not allowed
cases.paragraph: A number MUST NOT have a leading zero unless the value is zero.

cases.title: Object member names must be strings
cases.paragraph: An object member name is a string, which is quoted.

cases.title: Unescaped U+000A in a string is invalid
cases.paragraph: Unescaped control characters (U+0000 through U+001F) MUST NOT appear in a string.

cases.title: The empty document is not a JSON text
cases.paragraph: A JSON text is a serialized value (RFC 7159/8259) or object/array (RFC 4627).

cases.title: Two top-level values are not a single JSON text
cases.paragraph: A JSON text is one serialized value.

cases.title: Literal names are lowercase only
cases.paragraph: The literal names MUST be lowercase. No other literal names are allowed.

cases.title: RFC 8259 interchange encoding is UTF-8 only
cases.paragraph: JSON text exchanged between systems that are not part of a closed ecosystem MUST be encoded using UTF-8.

cases.title: The names within an object SHOULD be unique
cases.paragraph: The names within an object SHOULD be unique. When they are not, the behavior is unpredictable across implementations.
cases.notes: SHOULD, not MUST. Recording which value wins (first vs last) is useful; both accepting and taking one of the values is common.

cases.title: A proper UTF-16 surrogate pair in \u escapes
cases.paragraph: To escape a code point that is not in the Basic Multilingual Plane, the character may be represented as a twelve-character sequence encoding the UTF-16 surrogate pair.

cases.title: Unpaired surrogates are not Unicode scalar values
cases.paragraph: The hex escape form may represent unpaired surrogates; software that interprets JSON as Unicode text may reject them. I-JSON forbids them.
cases.notes: RFC 8259 does not forbid unpaired surrogates in the grammar; I-JSON does. Recorded as SHOULD NOT for interchange.
